name: Tie-dye
summary: A way to colour cloth in which parts are tied, folded or bound before the dye bath, so that the bound parts resist the dye.
how: Fold, twist or gather the wet cloth, and bind it with string or rubber bands.
Soak the cloth in a dye bath, or apply dye to each section.
Rinse, untie and dry the cloth; each piece shows a different pattern.

origin.note: Cloth with tied resist patterns, known as shibori, survives from Japan of the eighth century.

adoptions.via: American counterculture makers dye T-shirts and skirts at home, and wear them at concerts and festivals.
